primaryComponents: Outer shell (titanium alloy with PVD coating)
Integrated sensor array (multiple Photoplethysmography (PPG) LEDs including green, red, and infrared; multiple photodiodes; three Negative Temperature Coefficient (NTC) temperature sensors)
Flexible Printed Circuit Board (FPC) housing microcontrollers, signal processing unit, and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) module
operationalLogic: The Oura Ring Gen 3 is a passive, continuously-worn biometric sensor designed to fit on a finger. Its internal sensor array, comprising optical (PPG) and thermal (NTC) sensors, makes direct contact with the skin. The PPG LEDs emit light into the finger's capillaries, and photodiodes detect the reflected light to measure blood volume changes, enabling calculation of heart rate, heart rate variability, and blood oxygen saturation. NTC temperature sensors directly measure skin temperature. Accelerometer and gyroscope components detect motion, orientation, and subtle movements for activity tracking and sleep stage detection. All collected raw data is processed by the embedded FPC and transmitted wirelessly via Bluetooth Low Energy to a paired external device for further analysis. The device operates silently and without any moving parts, relying on its internal rechargeable battery, which is replenished through inductive charging.
maintenanceNodes: Outer casing (requires regular cleaning for hygiene and removal of superficial debris)
Inner sensor surface (requires cleaning to ensure optimal skin contact and accurate sensor readings)
Charging area (requires cleaning to maintain efficient inductive power transfer)
Embedded battery (non-user replaceable; subject to degradation over time affecting device autonomy and lifespan)
